topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Understanding Vectors

sections.title: Introduction: What is a Vector?
lecture_lines: Vectors are arrows representing direction and magnitude.
They can also be lists of numbers.
Think of them as positions in space.
animations: Create a 2D arrow at the origin labeled 'Vector v' in color #FF0000 alongside a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg].
Animate the arrow sliding to a new position.
Change the arrow's color to #00FF00 to show displacement and measure the distance using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg].

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule
lecture_lines: Vector addition uses the head-to-tail rule.
Place the second tail at the first head.
The result is a new, single vector.
animations: Show two vectors 'u' and 'v' starting at origin. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]
Move the tail of vector 'v' to the head of 'u'.
Draw a resultant vector 'u+v' from origin to 'v''s head. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching Space
lecture_lines: Scalars stretch or shrink a vector's length.
A negative scalar flips the direction.
The line's slope remains constant throughout.
animations: Show vector 'v' in color #FFFF00 using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg] to measure its magnitude.
Scale 'v' by factor 2 to double its length.
Scale 'v' by factor -1 to flip its direction as if influenced by a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magnet.svg].

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Basis vectors i-hat and j-hat span the space.
Every vector is a scaled combination of these.
Grid coordinates map directly to these scales.
animations: Show a vector 'v' as a combination of 'i' and 'j'.
Highlight the grid formed by 'i' and 'j' using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg].

sections.title: Conclusion and Application Summary
lecture_lines: Linear algebra is the language of motion.
It powers computer graphics and physics.
Models are just collections of many vectors.
animations: Fade in all vectors discussed: 'u', 'v', and 'u+v'. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/physics.svg]
Highlight the combined space formed by all linear combinations.
